name: Gravitar
drawing: TM-206 IC parts list, figure 3-8 (Game PCB Assembly)
notes: No component-location drawing has been read for this board. Every device on the map comes from the IC parts list in TM-206, taken where the 1st and 2nd printings agree — 73 designators agree between them with no split at all, and 68 of those are on the grid and carry a device name the guard will stand behind.

Both printings put every row under one figure heading, 'Figure 3-8 Gravitar Game PCB Assembly', and neither reports a collision. This manual documents one PCB, so no --figure split was needed — unlike Red Baron, whose manual covers two.

The grid spacing is nominal. The designators are what the parts list gives and those are real, but nothing here has measured the board, so the drawn positions are the standard 1in by 0.75in DIP grid the rest of this repo assumes.

Gravitar and Space Duel are the same Atari colour-vector hardware, and the two harvests were run independently from different manuals (TM-206 and TM-181). They share 62 grid positions and agree on 54 of them. That agreement is external evidence for both maps: nothing in either pipeline could have produced it by construction, because neither harvest can see the other's manual.
The row alphabet is A B C D E F H J K L M N P R — skipping G, I, O and Q, the Atari convention confirmed here on a 1982 board.
conflicts: Eight of the 62 positions Gravitar shares with Space Duel carry a different device: H3 (LS20 here, LS02 there), K6 (LS02 / LS139), L4 (LS08 / LS42), L9 (LS244 / LS251), N3 (LS157 / LS32), N9 (LS244 / LS251), R3 (LS157 / LS08) and R4 (LS32 / LS174). These are not treated as errors in either map. The two games are different products on a shared board family and are expected to differ somewhere; L9 and N9 differing the same way (LS244 against LS251) in particular looks like a real design difference rather than noise, since a bad read would not repeat itself identically at two positions. Nothing has been changed on either board on the strength of the other — settling them needs a physical board or a drawing.
Five designators appear in only one printing and are therefore not placed.
